from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The determinant measures scaling of area.",
            "Start with a unit square area.",
            "Apply a matrix transformation now.",
            "Observe the square become a parallelogram.",
            "The change in area is determinant."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Determinant: Scaling Factor", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define objects
        square = Square(side_length=2, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(square, 'C3')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        self.play(Create(square))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#33FF57"))
        parallelogram = Polygon(
            np.array([-1, -1, 0]), np.array([1, -1, 0]), 
            np.array([2, 1, 0]), np.array([0, 1, 0]),
            color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3
        )
        self.place_at_grid(parallelogram, 'C3')
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#3357FF"))
        self.play(Transform(square, parallelogram))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FF33FF"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Concept of Basis Vectors", [
            "Define basis vectors i and j.", 
            "Matrices are sets of transformation instructions.", 
            "Watch where i and j land."
        ])
        
        # Setup Axes
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-1, 3], y_range=[-1, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.add(axes)
        
        # Vectors
        i_vec = Vector(RIGHT, color="#33FF57")
        j_vec = Vector(UP, color="#33FF57")
        i_label = MathTex(r"\hat{i}", color="#33FF57").next_to(i_vec.get_end(), DOWN)
        j_label = MathTex(r"\hat{j}", color="#33FF57").next_to(j_vec.get_end(), LEFT)
        
        # Grouped for ease
        basis_group = VGroup(i_vec, j_vec, i_label, j_label)
        self.add(basis_group)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#33FF57"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        
        # Create transform effect
        new_i = np.array([2, 1, 0])
        new_j = np.array([0, 2, 0])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        
        i_vec_target = Vector(new_i, color="#FF5733")
        j_vec_target = Vector(new_j, color="#FF5733")
        
        self.play(
            i_vec.animate.put_start_and_end_on(ORIGIN, axes.c2p(*new_i)),
            j_vec.animate.put_start_and_end_on(ORIGIN, axes.c2p(*new_j)),
            i_label.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(*new_i) + DOWN*0.3),
            j_label.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(*new_j) + LEFT*0.3),
            i_vec.animate.set_color("#FF5733"),
            j_vec.animate.set_color("#FF5733"),
            i_label.animate.set_color("#FF5733"),
            j_label.animate.set_color("#FF5733")
        )
        
        # Draw area
        rect = Polygon(ORIGIN, axes.c2p(*new_i), axes.c2p(*(new_i + new_j)), axes.c2p(*new_j), 
                       fill_opacity=0.3, color="#FF5733")
        self.play(Create(rect))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Defining the Formula (2x2)", [
            "The 2x2 formula is ad-bc.",
            "Signed area accounts for orientation.",
            "Reflection reverses the cat's orientation.",
            "Flipped orientation gives negative results.",
            "The formula reflects this logic."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        matrix = MathTex(r"\begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix}", color="#3357FF")
        formula = MathTex(r"ad - bc", color="#FF33A1")
        
        self.place_at_grid(matrix, 'B2', scale_factor=1.5)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'E2', scale_factor=1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(matrix))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#3357FF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF33A1")
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Using simple shape to represent the cat reflection concept
        cat = Triangle(color=YELLOW).rotate(PI)
        self.place_at_grid(cat, 'B5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(cat))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        cat_flipped = Triangle(color=RED).flip(UP)
        self.place_at_grid(cat_flipped, 'E5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(cat, cat_flipped))
        self.lecture[3].set_color(RED)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        self.play(Indicate(formula))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Critical Edge Cases: Determinant = 0", [
            "What if the determinant is zero?",
            "Space collapses into a line.",
            "Information is lost forever."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        square = Square(side_length=2, color=BLUE).set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(square, 'C3', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        collapsed_line = Line(start=LEFT*2, end=RIGHT*2, color=GRAY).set_stroke(width=6)
        self.place_at_grid(collapsed_line, 'C3', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        area_label = Text("Area = 0", color=RED, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(area_label, 'D4', scale_factor=0.8)
        area_label.set_opacity(0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(FadeIn(square))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
                  self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(
            square.animate.stretch(0, 0),
            ReplacementTransform(square.copy(), collapsed_line),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.play(collapsed_line.animate.set_color("#808080"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
                  self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(FadeIn(area_label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Real-World Application", [
            "Non-zero determinant means it's invertible.",
            "Invertible matrices can undo changes.",
            "Zero determinants destroy data irreversibly."
        ])

        # Objects
        cube = Cube(side_length=1.5, fill_opacity=0.6, color=BLUE)
        label = Text("Volume = Det(A)", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        target = Circle(radius=0.3, color=GREEN).set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(cube, 'B2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(label, 'A2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(cube), Write(label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        cube_transform = cube.copy().scale(0.5).set_color(PURPLE)
        self.play(Transform(cube, cube_transform), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(RED)
        self.place_at_grid(target, 'E4', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Flash(target.get_center(), color=RED, line_length=0.3, num_lines=12), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(2)

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The Scaling Factor
sections.content: Start with a visual representation of a unit square. Introduce the determinant as a 'scaling factor' that describes how much the area changes after a linear transformation.
sections.example: Visualize a 2D square with area 1. Apply a matrix transformation; show the square morphing into a parallelogram. If the new area is 3, the determinant is 3.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of Basis Vectors
sections.content: Briefly define basis vectors i (1,0) and j (0,1). Explain that a matrix is simply a set of instructions for where these vectors land.
sections.example: Animation showing vector 'i' landing on (a, c) and 'j' landing on (b, d) to form the matrix [[a, b], [c, d]].

sections.title: Defining the Formula (2x2)
sections.content: Derive the determinant formula ad - bc. Use a visual 'signed area' approach to explain why flipping the orientation results in a negative determinant.
sections.example: A cat-shaped icon is transformed. If the matrix transformation flips the cat's left and right sides (reflection), the area becomes negative, indicating an orientation reversal.

sections.title: Critical Edge Cases: Determinant = 0
sections.content: Explain the geometric significance of a zero determinant: the transformation crushes the 2D space into a 1D line or a 0D point, losing information.
sections.example: Show a 2D robot icon being flattened into a single line; visually demonstrate that 'information is lost' because you cannot recover the original 2D shape.

sections.title: Summary & Real-World Application
sections.content: Wrap up by connecting the determinant to system solvability. If the determinant is non-zero, the transformation is invertible, allowing us to 'undo' the change.
sections.example: Use a 'Data Decoder' analogy: If the determinant is 0, the code is scrambled permanently (irreversible). If non-zero, the transformation can be reversed to reveal the original image.

[VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The square/parallelogram currently occupies C3, which creates visual tension with the lecture lines on the left. Fix: Line 59 & 77: self.place_at_grid(obj, 'D4', scale_factor=0.8) (line=59, object=square/parallelogram)

[VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The object is too close to the text margin, risking overlap with the text block during the transformation animation. Fix: Line 59 & 77: self.place_in_area(obj, 'C4', 'E5', scale_factor=0.75) (line=77, object=parallelogram)

[VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: Poor utilization of vertical space leads to the object being centered in a way that feels cramped horizontally. Fix: Line 59: self.place_at_grid(obj, 'C5', scale_factor=0.9) (line=59, object=square)

[VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The axes object occupies an excessive area (A1-F6), causing it to crowd the lecture space and appear disproportionately large. Fix: Line 56: self.place_in_area(axes, 'B3', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6) (line=56, object=axes)

[VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The vector labels 'i' and 'j' are placed too far from the axes origin, making them visually disconnected from the graphic. Fix: self.place_at_grid(i_label, 'B4', scale_factor=0.8); self.place_at_grid(j_label, 'C3', scale_factor=0.8) (line=57, object=labels i and j)

[VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The transformation triangle animation overlaps with the grid boundary area, potentially clipping visual information. Fix: self.place_in_area(triangle_shape, 'C4', 'E5', scale_factor=0.5) (line=58, object=triangle_shape)

[VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: The matrix and formula are currently placed too low and too far right, causing visual imbalance and potentially obstructing the flow of the lecture text. Fix: Line 59: self.place_at_grid(matrix, 'A3', scale_factor=1.2), Line 60: self.place_at_grid(formula, 'B3', scale_factor=1.2) (line=59, object=matrix and formula)

[VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: The cat and flipped cat assets are positioned in a way that risks obscuring the right-side margin, making them feel disconnected from the central formula. Fix: Line 75: self.place_at_grid(cat, 'A5', scale_factor=0.9), Line 82: self.place_at_grid(cat_flipped, 'B5', scale_factor=0.9) (line=75, object=cat and cat_flipped)

[VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: Poor grid utilization leads to excessive whitespace in the lower half of the screen, creating an off-balance layout relative to the fixed left-side text. Fix: self.place_in_area(visual_group, 'C2', 'F6', scale_factor=1.0) (line=0, object=overall visual elements)

[VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: Animation sequence centered on C3 causes visual occlusion of the left-side lecture notes. Fix: Line 56: self.place_at_grid(square, 'C5', scale_factor=0.6) (line=56, object=square)

[VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The collapsed line animation persists in the center of the screen, obscuring spatial clarity. Fix: Line 59: self.place_at_grid(collapsed_line, 'C5', scale_factor=0.6) (line=59, object=collapsed_line)

[VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: Area label at D4 is too close to the active animation zone, creating clutter. Fix: Line 62: self.place_at_grid(area_label, 'E5', scale_factor=0.8) (line=62, object=area_label)

[VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: The cube at B2 is positioned too close to the lecture notes on the left, creating visual clutter and potential encroachment. Fix: Line 61: self.place_at_grid(cube, 'C3', scale_factor=0.8) (line=61, object=cube)

[VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: The label at A2 is poorly centered relative to its object and competes with the title area. Fix: Line 62: self.place_at_grid(label, 'C2', scale_factor=0.7) (line=62, object=label)
